summary: Facepalm: Search for 2026-09-28 (window Sept 22–28). The search tool hit its usage limit partway through the run, so coverage is limited. I'm submitting one candidate. It's Montgomery County, MD, which was set aside on 2026-09-26 for having only one accepted source. There's a new fact since then: I found and opened the county Board of Elections' own 2026 statement (dated Sept 23, 2026; the page found last time was the 2024 one). That gives one official source plus one accepted news page, foxbaltimore.com. One risk for the verifier: the foxbaltimore page's canonical URL and publisher tag point to WJLA (wjla.com), which is not on the accepted list, though the page sits on the accepted foxbaltimore.com domain. I set aside several other election mistakes because there were no accepted sources or they were reported after the scan date. Genius: I have no genius candidates for 2026-09-28. Search and page-opening hit the tool limit partway through the scan. After that I could not open a second publisher's page for any in-window lead, and every lead had only one accepted source open (ScienceDaily). The one story with two publishers open was the Caltech quantum-simulator result, but its Nature paper and Caltech announcement are dated August 19, 2026, too old for the window. Several leads look worth checking in a rerun, each needing a second accepted source and a confirmed date (listed under passed): the Weill Cornell/HSS spinal-stenosis stem cells (Cell), the Oregon State study linking the Cascadia and San Andreas faults, the Mizzou sarcopenia mechanism (JCI), the ORNL neutron imaging of the Scotty T. rex rib, and the UC Berkeley Pompeii dating study (Science Advances). Pair published.
